sentences.text:
THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT Challenging judgment and award dated 02.06.2015 passed by Principal Senior Civil Judge and MACT at Kalaburagi (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC no.829/2011, this appeal is filed.
2.
Sri J. Augustin, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by insurer challenging award insofar as finding on liability.

It was submitted that in an accident that occurred on 08.02.2010, insured auto rickshaw bearing registration no.KA-32/A-5798 met with an accident when driver Somshekar was unable to control vehicle on seeing a lorry coming from opposite side and it turtled due to sudden turn.

It was submitted that before NC: 2023:KHC-K:6519 Tribunal,
though insurer had specifically contended that vehicle in question was uninsured and driver was not having driving licence to drive vehicle at time of accident, merely on ground that claimant had produced attested copy of his driving licence, fastened liability upon insurer.

It was submitted that evidence was led by insurer to establish that driver of auto rickshaw was charge sheeted for causing accident by driving vehicle without driving licence and without insurance and had pleaded guilty to such charge.
It was submitted that Exs.R2 and R3 would establish that on his plea, he was convicted for said offences.

It was therefore, submitted that observation of Tribunal that merely on charge sheet, non-possession of driving licence cannot be held established would be incorrect and therefore, sought for allowing appeal.
3. Respondent no.1-claimant and respondent no.2-owner are served, unrepresented.

2 NC: 2023:KHC-K:6519 4.

From above submission and since insurer is in appeal challenging fastening of liability upon insurer, point that would arise for consideration is:
"Whether finding of Tribunal holding insurer liable to pay compensation would call for interference?"
5.
On perusal of Exs.P1 and P1(a), it is seen that complaint is filed by claimant against driver and owner of vehicle.
Ex. P2

-charge sheet would indicate that they were prosecuted for commission of offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC R/w Sections 180, 181, 187 and 196 of Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'M.V. Act').
Ex.R3 would indicate that C.C.no.522/2010 was referred to Lok Adalath, wherein plea was recorded.

On accused pleading guilty, they were convicted for offences punishable under Sections 279, 337, 338 of IPC R/w Sections 180, 181, 187 and 196 of M.V. Act and as per Ex.R2, they were convicted for said offences and ordered to pay fine.
Ex.R2 would also indicate that fine amount was paid.
On perusal of impugned award, only reasons assigned by Tribunal for fastening liability upon insurer is that, charge sheet does not establish that driver did not have driving licence.

However, in instant case, apart from Ex.P2-charge sheet, insurer has produced Ex.R3 - order recording plea,
wherein driver and owner pleaded guilty and Ex.R2 - certified copy of order sheet in criminal case,
wherein they were convicted for offence including driving motor vehicle without valid driving licence.
Said evidence is not controverted.
Under such circumstances, award against insurer would be unsustainable.
Point for consideration is answered in affirmative.

Consequently, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed.
ii. Claim petition against appellant-insurer is dismissed.
iii.
It is held that claimant would be entitled to recover compensation from owner of vehicle i.e., respondent no.1 before Tribunal.
Amount in deposit is ordered to be refunded to appellant-insurer with accrued interest, if any.

Sd/-
